Vladimir Komarov was a Soviet cosmonaut who took part in the Soyuz 1 mission. Despite of multiple complaints of him and his replacement pilot Yuri Gagarin about the design errors of the Soyuz craft, Komarov agreed to pilot the first vessel. Though he succesfully made it into orbit, the solar panels of the craft failed to unfold, making it very difficult for the cosmonaut to properly orient the vessel for re-entry into the atmosphere. When he eventually managed to properly perform a re-entry into earth's atmosphere during his 19th orbit around earth, the vessel's drogue and main parachute failed, sending it crashing into the ground. Komarov supposedly spend his last living seconds screaming and cursing at the people who had forced him to pilot the flawed vessel, doubly so as some sources suggest he only took part in the flight at all because he knew Yuri Gagarin would face certain death if he would fly it in his place.
He took the bullet for Yuri and he deserves the same respect and reverence as any of the other space cowboys. They knew the risks they were taking and still went up in the pursuit of science.
